Analysis: Both hypotheses present innovative integrations of epitranscriptomics into the pathogenesis of hepatocellular carcinoma, yet they differ in approach. Hypothesis 1 is highly novel, linking hypoxia‐induced m6A modifications in dendritic cells to impaired cathepsin translation, immune evasion, and HCC initiation. However, its multi‐step cascade and the complexity of immune regulation make it less immediately testable without resolving several mechanistic details. In contrast, Hypothesis 2—focusing on FTO‐mediated site‐specific m6A demethylation in NAFLD hepatocytes to promote metabolic reprogramming—is grounded in existing knowledge of FTO’s involvement in metabolic pathways. Its proposed mechanism, while still in need of additional specificity, appears more amenable to established molecular and cellular assays, thereby enhancing testability. Both are conceived with preclinical safety in mind, but the relative simplicity of experimental validation gives Hypothesis 2 an edge in terms of plausibility and immediate research translation.
